body:
Hm, this is the right place for the fix and I agree that the current code here is what introduces the bug. That is, `custom_overlay` should not have its `texture_filter` set to `TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE` since its parent obviously isn't in the scene tree. 

~~However, I believe this hardcoded fix doesn't allow for the tile previews to inherit the `texture_filter` setting of TileMapLayer's ancestor nodes. Instead, the previews will *always* use whatever is set in Project Settings (Project Settings > Rendering > Textures > Canvas Textures > Default Texture Filter) instead of inheriting from parent's `texture_filter` as expected / intended. It looks like we were working on PRs for this at the same time so I'll post my followup.~~

I agree that the overlay needs an explicit filter resolved from the edited scene. Regarding ancestor inheritance, doesn’t `edited_layer -> get_texture_filter_in_tree()` already resolve explicit filters on CanvasItem ancestors? The viewport fallback only runs if that result is still TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE, so I think those ancestor settings are preserved. I did test commit 43c962e108 and found a related case: a SubViewportContainer set to `Nearest -> SubViewport` set to `Inherit -> TileMapLayer` set to Inherit. The placed tiles are sharp, but the preview is blurry. Changing only the SubViewport to explicit Nearest makes the preview sharp; undoing it makes the preview blurry again. It seems the remaining issue is that get_default_canvas_item_texture_filter() returns the viewport’s configured Inherit value rather than its resolved filter. Would using the viewport’s get_texture_filter_in_tree() address this? Minimal reproduction attached. Happy to test your approach against this case too. [pr-123692-viewport-inherit-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32495518/pr-123692-viewport-inherit-mrp.zip)

> However, I believe this hardcoded fix doesn't allow for the tile previews to inherit the `texture_filter` setting of TileMapLayer's ancestor nodes. Instead, the previews will _always_ use whatever is set in Project Settings (Project Settings > Rendering > Textures > Canvas Textures > Default Texture Filter) instead of inheriting from parent's `texture_filter` as expected / intended. It looks like we were working on PRs for this at the same time so I'll post my followup.

Thanks for the feedback!
It does check its ancestry, get_texture_filter_in_tree() calls _refresh_texture_filter_cache() which has this line:
`texture_filter_cache = parent_item->texture_filter_cache;`

I dont recall the exact mechanism rn but that texture filter is lazy loaded from its ancestors, so it is always up to date. So we can be sure that if get_texture_filter_in_tree() returns TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE is because no ancestor has a different value.

Look that the switch is only used when the filter equals TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE, that would be in the only possible case: every ancestor has filter = inherit, so we need to check the tilemaplayer's viewport in order to get the explicit filter value, and without checking its ancestry.

> It does check its ancestry, get_texture_filter_in_tree() calls _refresh_texture_filter_cache() which has this line:
texture_filter_cache = parent_item->texture_filter_cache;

I initially thought it only checks 1 parent deep, but after spending further time in the debugger I believe you're correct! There's no need for a loop walking upwards through the parents (as in my PR) when `texture_filter_cache` achieves the inheritance for us.

> It seems the remaining issue is that get_default_canvas_item_texture_filter() returns the viewport’s configured Inherit value rather than its resolved filter. Would using the viewport’s get_texture_filter_in_tree() address this?

As @gabcont said, if `get_texture_filter_in_tree()` returns `TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE`, then we don't want the resolved filter (there is none), we want whatever the default value is, so I think the code is correct as it is in this PR.

In summary, this looks good to me! I also tested your version and it works.

Thanks for taking another look! I think the SubViewport case I mentioned may still be an issue, though. With: `SubViewportContainer (Nearest) -> SubViewport (Inherit) -> TileMapLayer (Inherit)` the placed tiles are sharp, but the tile preview is blurry: For comparison, placing the TileMapLayer directly under the SubViewportContainer makes both the placed tiles and the preview sharp: Changing only the SubViewport from `Inherit` to explicit `Nearest` also makes the preview sharp, and undoing that change makes it blurry again. This makes me think the SubViewport's effective texture filter is resolving to `Nearest`, while the preview is still seeing the configured `Inherit` value. My understanding is that `get_default_canvas_item_texture_filter()` returns the Viewport's configured value (`Inherit` here), while `get_texture_filter_in_tree()` returns the inherited/effective value (`Nearest` here). So I think this specific case may still need to use the resolved filter. Does that make sense?

> I think the SubViewport case I mentioned may still be an issue, though.

Yes I'm seeing the issue now and just reproduced it. I think the change you mentioned in your first comment would fix it:
```
edited_layer_vp->get_default_canvas_item_texture_filter() 
=> 
edited_layer_vp->get_texture_filter_in_tree()
```
(and change the switch cases to be the RSE:CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER enum instead of the CanvasItem::TextureFilter enum)

However... something I noticed while testing this fix is that `Viewport::_refresh_texture_filter_cache` has this block:

```
default_canvas_item_texture_filter_cache = (RenderingServerEnums::CanvasItemTextureFilter)parent_ci->get_texture_filter_in_tree();
if (default_canvas_item_texture_filter_cache == RSE::CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_DEFAULT) {
    default_canvas_item_texture_filter_cache = RSE::CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR;
}
```

I'm not sure that the cache should be set to LINEAR in this case. This line of code breaks our fix by hardcoding LINEAR here, when it should probably be another switch statement to set the cache by reading whatever the current value in ProjectSettings is. (It's starting to feel like conversion helper functions between all these enums would be helpful)

> I'm not sure that the cache should be set to LINEAR in this case. This line of code breaks our fix by hardcoding LINEAR here, when it should probably be another switch statement to set the cache by reading whatever the current value in ProjectSettings is. (It's starting to feel like conversion helper functions between all these enums would be helpful)

@radioactivejackal1414 Thanks for digging into this. That `LINEAR` fallback made me look through the related Viewport issues, which is how I found #119462.

I dug into that behavior a bit further and opened #123746 to address the Viewport inheritance side of it. It handles the case where an inheriting Viewport's parent `CanvasItem` still resolves to the viewport default, as well as cases with ordinary `Node` instances between Viewports.

I think this addresses the underlying fallback you ran into here. With that fixed, `edited_layer_vp->get_texture_filter_in_tree()` should be able to provide the resolved filter without needing to read `ProjectSettings` directly here.

I read @fsfgrafb's #123746 and agree that this issue must be solved on top of those fixes in viewports inheritance. 

That @radioactivejackal1414's change would be the fix, however I dont know what is the correct way of handling a PR blocked by another in this project as this is my first time here, should I rebase my branch on top of #123746? If anyone knows the procedure please let me know and I'll apply the changes. Thx in advance
